summary: Iteration 83 — Slangcart push-notification pipeline audit. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases green in tests/test_iter83_push_pipeline.py (evidence trail, RBAC, register-push fingerprinting, multi-device, opt-out prefs, in-app system intact) + all 5 direct-Mongo pipeline checks green in tests/iter83_direct_pipeline.py (channel routing per kind, legacy channel remap, opted_out logging, new-device duplicate protection, in-app row still written) + owner regression scripts verify_phase1_money.py 56/56 and verify_phase2_returns.py 81/81. Evidence pipeline is real: POST /api/push/test returns ok=false / relay='key_missing' / relay_http_status=401 / relay_response='{"error":"invalid X-Push-Key"}' / stage='rejected' / channel_id='orders_v2' / key_configured=false with a human hint, exactly as the owner asked. GET /api/admin/push/diagnostics reports verdict='relay_key_missing', channels orders='orders_v2'/chat='chat_v2'/legacy_remap={chat:chat_v2,default:orders_v2}, totals by_stage/by_result, relay_probe {reachable:true,http_status:401,body:'{"error":"invalid X-Push-Key"}'}, recent_sends[] each with stage/result/http_status/channel_id/category/upstream_body. GET /api/admin/push/diagnostics/user returns notification_prefs, push_registration, devices[], recent_sends[] and in_app_notifications count; unknown email → 404. RBAC hardened: buyer, vendor, scoped products_manager and anonymous all rejected on /push/test, /admin/push/diagnostics and /admin/push/diagnostics/user. POST /api/register-push rejects user_id≠JWT with 403, records ONE row per (user, token_fingerprint) — verified TWO device rows persist for two different fake tokens for the same buyer (multi-device confirmed), the raw token is NEVER stored anywhere (deep string-scan of the device rows for the raw tokens found zero hits — only the fingerprint 'sha256prefix…LAST6 (N chars)' representation is kept). Channel routing via core.notifications.create_notification confirmed at the DB level: kinds order/announcement/security/vendor/cashback → orders_v2, kind chat → chat_v2; explicit legacy channel_id 'chat' → chat_v2 and 'default' → orders_v2. Opt-out proven by flipping notification_prefs.orders=false and firing a categorised send: push_log row is stage='skipped', result='opted_out' and nothing was handed to the relay. Duplicate protection proven: fresh new-device sign-in for testbuyer produced exactly ONE push_log row (title 'New device signed in', category 'login_alerts', channel orders_v2) AND ONE in-app db.notifications row of kind 'security' — the previous behaviour of two push rows for one login is fixed by core/login_history.py passing push=False into create_notification. Frontend (mobile 390×844): /admin/push-diagnostics renders the amber verdict banner 'Relay key not injected yet' with body 'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is still \'placeholder\'…', the Pipeline card with Relay key injected='No — placeholder', Relay host reachable='Yes (HTTP 401)', Send attempts=106, Accepted=0, Rejected=106, Registered devices=2, Android channel (orders)=orders_v2, Android channel (chat)=chat_v2, the 'Send a test push' form with target email input, and the 'Last 50 send attempts' list showing every attempt with stage/result/HTTP 401/channel/category and the literal relay body '{"error":"invalid X-Push-Key"}'. Tapping 'Send test push' triggers a real relay call and the UI shows Result='Not delivered (key_missing)', Relay HTTP status=401, Relay response='{"error":"invalid X-Push-Key"}', Channel used='orders_v2' — never a fake success. 'Check this account' with testbuyer@test.com renders that user's Devices and last sends; with a bogus email the readable 'No user with that email' error is shown and the page does not crash. Admin bottom nav is still exactly 6 tabs (Home · Users · Shop · Payouts · Wallet · More); /admin/returns and /admin/push-diagnostics are reachable only from /admin/more (both present in the more list). Buyer /notifications is untouched — it lists 'New device signed in', 'Refund credited', 'Cashback adjusted', 'Return approved', 'Order delivered', '₹50 cashback credited', 'Order placed!' … normally.

react_native_issues.issue: Web-only warning '[expo-notifications] Listening to push token changes is not yet fully supported on web. Adding a listener will have no effect.' — harmless in this Expo web preview because src/push.ts already short-circuits Platform.OS==='web' before requesting a token; the token-rotation listener attempt is what emits the warning. Reference: /app/frontend/src/push.ts:105 (attachTokenListener). Optional cleanup: also guard attachTokenListener with Platform.OS!=='web' inside registerForPush to silence the log. Not a functional bug.
Repeated web console warning '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"'. Pre-existing across the app, not introduced by this push change.
Repeated web console warning 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Pre-existing, not from this change.

action_items: Optional: silence the '[expo-notifications] Listening to push token changes is not yet fully supported on web' warning by wrapping attachTokenListener() in a Platform.OS!=='web' guard inside src/push.ts (the whole registerForPush already returns early on web, but attachTokenListener is still callable from the token-changed path). Cosmetic only.
No blocking bugs. The pipeline audit passes and every piece of evidence the owner demanded is now real and provable.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/push.py:send_push — every send takes exactly one push_log write with a distinct `stage` (created→sent_to_relay→accepted|rejected|skipped|chunked), the relay's raw HTTP status and body are persisted verbatim (upstream_body truncated to 400 chars) — this is the exact 'proof that separates server didn't send / Firebase rejected / phone never registered' the owner asked for.

routes/push.py:token_fingerprint — sha256 prefix + last 6 chars + length string. The raw token never touches Mongo. Verified by scanning every string field of the device row for the raw token substring; zero hits. Matches the playbook 'SuprSend owns tokens' rule while still giving the owner something to compare.

core/notifications.py — kind→category map (order/vendor→orders, chat→chats, announcement/promo→offers, security→login_alerts) is centralised. This is what actually makes the opt-out enforceable at the send helper.

core/login_history.py — the new-device branch now passes push=False into create_notification and does the tray push exclusively through the explicit send_push call (category='login_alerts', idempotency_key='newdev-<id>'). Direct test confirms exactly ONE push_log row per new-device sign-in.

routes/push.py:CHANNEL_BY_CATEGORY / LEGACY_CHANNEL_MAP — orders/offers/login_alerts/vendor_new_order all land on orders_v2; 'chats' on chat_v2. Legacy 'chat' and 'default' are transparently remapped so no call-site can accidentally target a frozen-importance channel on the device.

routes/push.py:register_push — RegisterPushBody strips the 6 diagnostic fields (app_ownership/is_device/os_version/device_name/app_version/permission_status) before relay_body is built; they're kept only in push_devices for local diagnostics. Correct separation of concerns.

frontend/src/push.ts — addPushTokenListener re-registers on FCM/APNs rotation; the 'same user, same token' guard now also compares the token, not just the user id, so a rotated token is actually re-sent. The web bundle should probably also skip attachTokenListener() to silence the expo warning, but functionality is correct.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Push pipeline evidence trail lives in TWO collections: db.push_log (one row per send attempt, stage/result/http_status/upstream_body/channel_id/category/recipients/idempotency_key) and db.push_devices (one row per user+token_fingerprint, upstream_status/upstream_body/app_ownership/is_device/os_version/device_name/app_version/permission_status/registrations count). EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY in /app/backend/.env is intentionally 'placeholder' — DO NOT change it. The relay must answer 401 'invalid X-Push-Key'; anything else in this env is a regression. Admin push diagnostics endpoints: /api/push/test (POST, super_admin, body={title?,message?,target_email?,channel_id?}), /api/admin/push/diagnostics?limit=50, /api/admin/push/diagnostics/user?email=…. Buyer/vendor endpoints for notification prefs: GET/PUT /api/me/notification-prefs. Register push: POST /api/register-push {user_id,platform,device_token,+6 diagnostics}. Admin bottom nav is locked to Home/Users/Shop/Payouts/Wallet/More (see /app/frontend/app/admin/_layout.tsx) — do not add another Tabs.Screen without href:null.
rca_of_issue: Bug: in-app notifications recorded but never appeared in Android tray. Two root causes identified and fixed by the main agent (this iteration only validates them): (1) The pre-existing Android notification channels 'default' and 'chat' were created at a LOWER importance on the owner's phone by earlier builds; Android freezes importance at channel creation, so raising it in app code after the fact has no effect. Fix: NEW channel ids orders_v2 / chat_v2 created at MAX importance at app boot (frontend/app/_layout.tsx), backend routes/push.py fills channel_id centrally (CHANNEL_BY_CATEGORY) and remaps legacy 'chat'/'default' → v2 (LEGACY_CHANNEL_MAP). Confirmed at the DB level: 6 kinds routed correctly and both legacy names remap. (2) send_push() previously returned a status string that call-sites discarded — there was ZERO evidence of what the relay actually answered, so 'server never sent' / 'Firebase rejected' / 'phone never registered' were indistinguishable. Fix: every attempt is now written to push_log with the exact relay HTTP status and body, every registration to push_devices with a non-reversible token_fingerprint, and /api/push/test / /api/admin/push/diagnostics return that evidence verbatim. Confirmed by 14 API tests + 5 direct-Mongo tests + live UI validation. Bonus fixes verified: (a) core/login_history.py's double-push (once via create_notification, once via explicit send_push) now emits exactly ONE push_log row per new-device sign-in — verified with a direct record_login call and push_log count. (b) frontend/src/push.ts now re-registers on token rotation via addPushTokenListener and its cache key is (user_id, token) not just user_id. Reproduction (from a clean checkout with EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder): (i) log in as support@slangcart.com, GET /api/admin/push/diagnostics → verdict='relay_key_missing', relay_probe.reachable=true+http_status=401. (ii) POST /api/push/test → ok=false, relay='key_missing', relay_http_status=401, relay_response contains 'invalid X-Push-Key'. (iii) On the admin app open /admin/more → 'Push notification diagnostics' → tap 'Send test push' → UI shows 'Not delivered (key_missing)' + HTTP 401 + relay body — never a fake success. Mitigation once the real relay key is injected at deploy: verdict flips through no_device_registered → relay_rejecting → pipeline_healthy as devices come online and sends land.
